 What's open and what's closed in Minnesota on Veterans Day 2026
 Dustin Nelson 2026년 11월 8일 일 오후 1:34 UTC 0 (Photo by Leonardo Silva on Unsplash) Veterans Day, which always lands on Nov. 11, is coming on Wednesday. 
 With the holiday taking place in the middle of the week, it’ll mean there are closures to be aware of. Here’s a look at what businesses and services will be closed in Minnesota this year. 
 Post Office and other delivery services
 The U.S. Postal Service is closed in observance of Veterans Day. UPS operates normally, and FedEx has modified service.
 Government services
 Government offices and services are largely closed on Veterans Day. That includes federal and state courts, as well as federal, county, and city offices.
 Metro Transit and other transit services
 Most public transportation, including Metro Transit in the Twin Cities, runs on a regular schedule for Veterans Day. 
 Garbage collection
 Garbage collection procedures will vary between cities and services, but service in Minneapolis and St. Paul will remain on schedule for the holiday. 
 Advertisement
 Parking
 On-street parking meters in Minneapolis and St. Paul are free on Veterans Day. However, not all meters in the Twin Cities are operated by the city. The University of Minnesota and Minneapolis Parks and Recreation operate their own meters. 
 Banks
 It’s a Federal Reserve holiday, so banks will be closed. That includes Citibank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Affinity Plus Federal Credit Union, Huntington Bank, and U.S. Bank locations.
 Malls, stores, and restaurants
 Most malls, stores, and restaurants are open on Veterans Day. Many businesses also offer discounts or free meals for veterans and active military personnel as part of the holiday. 
 Libraries
 Most libraries will be closed, including the  Hennepin County,  Ramsey County , the  Duluth Public Library ,  St. Paul Public Library , and  Rochester Public Library systems.
 Honoring veterans
 In 2026, the state’s official Veterans Day celebration will be hosted by the Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs at the Duluth National Guard Training and Community Center. 
 Doors for the event open at 8:30 a.m. and begin with a community breakfast. The program begins at 10 a.m. and features an honor guard, live music, and remarks from a keynote speaker and elected officials.
